Package neqsim.process.measurementdevice

Class AnalyserSampleSystem

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.AnalyserSampleSystem
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class AnalyserSampleSystem extends Object implements Serializable
Screening model of an extractive moisture-analyser sample system (probe, heat-traced tube, pressure regulator, analyser cell).

The class answers the questions that decide whether a water dew point analyser reading is a process value or a sample-system artefact after a shutdown and restart:

  • does water, hydrocarbon or glycol condense in the sample tube or cabinet at a given tube temperature;
  • how long does the sample take to travel from the process tap to the cell (transport lag);
  • how long does a liquid water film take to evaporate into the dry sample flow (dry-out time);
  • how long does a glycol (TEG) film take to evaporate (persistence of a glycol film on tubing or sensor).

Water content and water dew point use the Bukacek correlation (same as WaterDewPointAnalyser default). The hydrocarbon dew point uses a NeqSim dew point temperature flash on the water- and glycol-free gas. The glycol vapour content uses the component vapour pressure (ideal Raoult, enhancement factor neglected), which makes the glycol dry-out time an upper bound at high pressure and close to exact at the near-atmospheric analyser cell. Flows are in normal litres per hour (0 C, 1.01325 bara). The film evaporation model assumes the sample gas leaving the film location is saturated at the film temperature (maximum evaporation capacity), so the dry-out times are lower bounds for a given film mass.

1.0

    • getWaterFilmDryOutTimeHours

      public double getWaterFilmDryOutTimeHours(double filmMassKg, double filmTemperatureC, double filmPressureBara, double flowNlPerHour)
      Time to evaporate a liquid water film into the sample flow. The gas passing the film is assumed to leave saturated at the film temperature and pressure (maximum evaporation capacity), so the result is a lower bound.
      Parameters:
      filmMassKg - mass of liquid water in the film in kg
      filmTemperatureC - film temperature in C
      filmPressureBara - pressure at the film in bara
      flowNlPerHour - sample flow passing the film in Nl/h
      Returns:
      dry-out time in hours (infinite if the gas is already saturated)

    • getSaturatedGlycolMoleFraction

      public double getSaturatedGlycolMoleFraction(double temperatureC, double pressureBara)
      Glycol vapour mole fraction of a gas in equilibrium with liquid glycol at the given temperature and pressure.

      Calculated with a two-phase TP flash of the dry sample gas with an excess of glycol, using the equation of state of the sample gas (use a CPA system for glycols). The component vapour-pressure correlation is only used as a fallback if the flash does not give a liquid glycol phase, because tabulated glycol vapour-pressure coefficients can be unreliable far below the normal boiling point.

      Parameters:
      temperatureC - temperature in C
      pressureBara - pressure in bara
      Returns:
      glycol vapour mole fraction (-), NaN if it cannot be calculated
